introduction_markdown:
This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C. Section A: answer ALL 5 questions; you will be graded for the best 4 answers. Section B: answer ALL 2 questions in this section using the spaces provided; both questions carry equal marks. Section C: answer ONLY TWO questions out of three; if you attempt more than 2 questions, only the first two will be considered. Where appropriate, equations and diagrams should be used to illustrate your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

**Useful data:** specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g$^{-1}$ $^\circ$C$^{-1}$; 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 cm$^3$.
enonce_intro_markdown: A farmer tested a soil sample that had a pH of 4.5 and was deficient in one of the main elements needed for crop yield.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) State the three main elements needed for crop yield.

(ii) Give one chemical substance that contains all 3 elements. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) The three main elements (primary nutrients) are **nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P) and potassium (K)**.

(ii) An **NPK fertiliser** (a compound fertiliser, for example one labelled NPK 15-15-15) contains all three elements.

questions.enonce_markdown:
You are given the following nitrogenous fertilisers: $\mathrm{NH_4NO_3}$ and $\mathrm{(NH_4)_2SO_4}$

(i) Give the name of the fertiliser $\mathrm{(NH_4)_2SO_4}$

(ii) Which of the two fertilizers has a higher nitrogen content?

Show how you arrived at your answer. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) $\mathrm{(NH_4)_2SO_4}$ is **ammonium sulphate**.

(ii) Compare the percentage of nitrogen by mass in each fertiliser (N = 14, H = 1, O = 16, S = 32).

- $\mathrm{NH_4NO_3}$: relative formula mass $= 14 + 4(1) + 14 + 3(16) = 80$. It contains 2 nitrogen atoms: $\%\,\mathrm{N} = \dfrac{28}{80} \times 100 = 35.0\%$.
- $\mathrm{(NH_4)_2SO_4}$: relative formula mass $= 2(14 + 4) + 32 + 4(16) = 132$. It contains 2 nitrogen atoms: $\%\,\mathrm{N} = \dfrac{28}{132} \times 100 = 21.2\%$.

**Ammonium nitrate, $\mathrm{NH_4NO_3}$, has the higher nitrogen content** ($35.0\%$ against $21.2\%$).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) What does a pH of 4.5 indicate about the soil?

(ii) Suggest a substance that can be used to raise the pH of the soil. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) A pH of 4.5 is below 7: the soil is **acidic**.

(ii) **Lime** can be added to neutralise the acidity and raise the pH: calcium hydroxide (slaked lime), calcium oxide (quicklime) or calcium carbonate (limestone). Example: $\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2 + 2H^+ \rightarrow Ca^{2+} + 2H_2O}$.
